what: Per-model specification cards for the tractor units this system appraises. Read into the identity and close-up prompts so the vision model knows what specific truck it is looking at, not merely that it is a truck.
why: The only model-specific thing in the pipeline used to be a string. `passes.vehicle_line` turned the identity read into one sentence and that sentence was everything passes B, C and D knew about the vehicle. A 2015 Ford Cargo tractor and a 2023 F-MAX at the same odometer received the same reference for what 'on schedule' looks like, the same component checklist and the same expectations.
basis: Two kinds of row, labelled separately and never mixed. `corpus` blocks are computed from data/metadata/sources/tr_truckmarket.jsonl and are facts about this dataset, not about the model in general. Everything else is hand-curated from the cited sources and carries the same contract as data/reference/new_prices_tr.json - a URL, a date and a source_type per model. Spec, generations, weak points and identity tells were researched against the cited sources. Spec, generations, weak points and identity tells were researched against the cited sources. Spec, generations, weak points and identity tells were researched against the cited sources.
no_prices: This file is read into a prompt. app/modelspec.py:assert_priceless walks it on load and raises on anything that reads as a currency figure, because 'the VLM never sees or emits a price' is the separation that makes this system more than a thin wrapper. Say what a component does and how it fails, never what it costs.
refresh: Hand-curated and stamped, the same posture as USD_TRY in app/config.py and the rows in new_prices_tr.json. Re-check the source URLs and update as_of; app.cli doctor reports the age and how many models actually carry a citation.

models.segment: long-haul flagship tractor unit; International Truck of the Year 2019
models.cab: Cab-over-engine (COE). One cab only across the tractor range: a 2.5 m full-width high-roof sleeper with a flat floor and up to two bunks - there is no day cab and no low-roof F-MAX, so a low-roofed Ford tractor is NOT an F-MAX. Ford Otosan sells it as F-MAX (4x2), F-MAX L, and F-MAX LL (tandem rear axle), all on the same cab. A limited F-MAX Select edition of 400 units was launched in 2022.
models.driveline: Ford Otosan Ecotorq 12.7 L inline-six Euro 6 diesel, 3,600 mm wheelbase, 600 L aluminium fuel tank. Launch specification (2018 onward): 500 PS / 2,500 Nm, 12-speed ZF Traxon automated gearbox. New F-MAX (2025 model-year update): Ecotorq GEN2 rated 510 PS / 2,600 Nm with a 16-speed automated gearbox Ford calls 'Ecotorq 16S 2600 OD'. Automated gearbox throughout - a manual F-MAX is not offered.

visual_markers: Front grille is a large dark/black panel with four horizontal slat openings, contrasting against the body colour - it is NOT painted in the cab colour (the body-coloured grille arrived with the 2025 update)
Blue Ford oval badge sits centred inside the grille, on the upper slat
Headlamp bezels are body-coloured or silver, not black
Conventional glass door mirrors: a large main mirror housing plus a smaller wide-angle housing, carried on tubular arms, one pair each side
'F-MAX' lettering across the lower bumper, below the grille
A small power badge ('500') on the upper cab side just behind the door shut line
'FORD TRUCKS' wordmark with a small red-and-white Ford Trucks logo block on the chassis side skirt below the door

generations.years: 2025-present (Ford Trucks calls it the New F-MAX)
visual_markers: Front grille surround is painted in the body colour and blends into the cab panel; the black slat openings sit inside a body-coloured frame
'F-MAX' lettering has moved UP onto the body-coloured panel directly above the grille slats (on the 2018 car it was on the lower bumper)
Headlamps sit in black bezels as standard, with a white LED daytime-running strip running down the outer edge and along the bottom of each lamp
New 'ceramic view' Ford badge in the grille

Digital Mirror System: slim camera arms and a small wedge-shaped camera pod at the top of each A-pillar in place of the large glass mirror housings - the single most reliable way to date a photo of an F-MAX
Black band across the top of the cab front with a pair of small LED marker lamps at each end
Interior: 12-inch all-digital instrument cluster and a 12.4-inch central multimedia screen; a 7-inch touch control panel beside the bunk

known_weak_points.note: Ecotorq 12.7 oil consumption and turbocharger failure are the most repeated owner complaints on 2021-2023 trucks, several escalating to bottom-end work (bearings, pistons, liners, rings). One owner attributes piston seizure at roughly 220,000 km to debris from the engine oil cooler entering the oil circuit. Look for a recently cleaned or freshly painted engine, new hose clips, and a turbo/oil-cooler area that is noticeably cleaner than its surroundings.

Repeated coolant-hose bursts and oil/water leaks after engine work are among the most frequently reported F-MAX problems. Check for dried coolant staining around hose joints, and for a fresh oil film on the sump, oil cooler and gearbox bellhousing.

Air leaks from the rear suspension bellows on the tractor are reported at around 80,000 km, alongside air-conditioning faults. Check the bags for chafing, perishing and for a sagging or unevenly seated rear end in a side-on photograph.
An owner report under warranty describes the air compressor passing oil and water into the air system. Check the tanks and drain valves for oily residue.
Exhaust and emissions faults, including exhaust replacement, are reported on low-mileage trucks. A brand-new exhaust or DPF canister on an otherwise weathered chassis is worth noting.
In-cab display failures are reported while still under warranty; a blank, replaced or aftermarket-looking screen is a flag on a truck of this age.
Drivers report the standard seats are hard and the ride harsh over broken surfaces, so seat base and bolster wear can look advanced for the mileage.

identity_tells: Very tall, near-vertical two-box front: a deep body-coloured panel carrying a full-width slatted grille, with a one-piece wraparound bumper below it
Blue Ford oval badge on the grille centreline - Ford Otosan's heavy trucks wear the car company's oval, not a separate truck emblem
'F-MAX' in widely letter-spaced capitals on the front (lower bumper pre-2025, above the grille from 2025)
Headlamp clusters are tall vertical units set into the outer lower corners of the bumper, not horizontal lamps in the cab face
One cab silhouette only: full-width high roof with a straight roofline and an integrated roof deflector - the F-MAX has no low-roof or day-cab body
'FORD TRUCKS' on the chassis side skirt and a Ford Trucks logo block; on Turkish listings the make is often typed as 'TRUCKS' because of this badge

models.segment: mid-range and long-haul tractor unit, Ford Otosan's tractor before and alongside the F-MAX. In Turkish listings these are frequently typed as make 'TRUCKS' because the chassis and dealer signage carry the FORD TRUCKS wordmark rather than 'Cargo'.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine (COE). The model number decodes as GVW in tonnes + power in tens of PS + T for cekici (tractor): 1846T = 18 t, 460 PS, tractor. The 2012-onward tractor uses a raised-roof sleeper cab with 1,945 mm interior height (220 mm taller than the 1838T it replaced), cab air suspension, wide steps, roof deflector, folding side deflectors and side skirts. Ford Otosan offers a standard version with a 1,200 mm fifth-wheel height and a lower 'Midilli' version for high-cube trailers - the Midilli sits visibly lower on smaller-diameter tyres. The current F-LINE 1845T is listed with an Extra High Roof OR a Low Roof sleeper cab, so unlike the F-MAX this family does have a low-roof body.
models.driveline: Four tractor generations on one basic cab structure, 2003-2019 (Cargo) and 2022-present (F-LINE). Cargo 1830 (300 PS) and 1838T (9.0 L Ecotorq, 380 PS, Euro 4/5) came first. The 2012-launched 1846T uses an FPT (Iveco) Cursor 10.3 L six, 460 PS at 2,100 rpm and 2,100 Nm from 1,050-1,550 rpm, VGT turbo, SCR Euro 5, 282 kW engine brake, offered with a manual OR an automated gearbox with an integrated 500 kW four-stage intarder; disc brakes, EBS and ESP standard; 60,000 km service interval. The 2016 Euro 6 1848T returns to Ford Otosan's own Ecotorq 12.7 L at 480 PS / 2,500 Nm (1,000-1,200 rpm) and adds the then-mandatory AEBS and lane-departure warning. A 420 PS 12.7 L Euro 6 version was also sold (1842T). The current F-LINE 1845T uses the Ecotorq GEN2 12.7 L at 450 PS / 2,300 Nm with a 16-speed automated 'Ecotorq 16S 2600 DD' gearbox, 3,600 mm wheelbase, 600 L aluminium tank.

visual_markers: Same basic cab shell as the later trucks but with the pre-2012 front end and the lower, shallower roof - interior height is 220 mm lower than the 2012 redesign, which in a side-on photograph reads as a shorter cab box above the windows
Lacks the body-coloured blisters over the front wheel arches that the 2012 redesign introduced

generations.years: 2012-2019 (1846T from 2013, 1848T from 2016, 1842T) - this is the body the 'TRUCKS'-badged Turkish listings almost always show
visual_markers: Blue Ford oval badge mounted HIGH on the body-coloured cab panel, above the grille - the opposite of the F-MAX, which carries its oval inside the grille. This one detail separates a Cargo tractor from an F-MAX in almost any front photograph
Grille is a black honeycomb-mesh panel, roughly trapezoidal, set low in the cab face and running straight into a large dark-grey bumper
Twin ROUND headlamps per side, stacked vertically in a black bezel at the outer lower corners: a larger main lamp above a smaller lamp. The F-MAX by contrast has tall rectangular lamp clusters
A body-coloured blister/bulge above each front wheel arch on the cab side
Dark-grey plastic bumper with a body-coloured lower lip, a centre step and licence-plate recess, and a pair of small round auxiliary lamps low in the centre
Black band across the top of the windscreen
Vertical black air-intake duct at the rear corner of the cab side
Interior: ice-blue backlit instrument cluster; the park brake control is integrated into the instrument panel rather than standing on the floor or console

generations.years: 2022 announced, on sale from February 2024 (1845T and the road/construction F-LINE models)
visual_markers: Renewed grille, bumper, headlights, front fenders, door and mirror trims over the 2012 Cargo body, styled to echo the F-MAX - but the cab structure and proportions are still the Cargo's, not the F-MAX's
Badged F-LINE / 1845T rather than Cargo
Interior: 9-inch multimedia display, new steering wheel and control buttons, new seat materials

known_weak_points.note: The 1846T's bought-in FPT Cursor 10.3 Euro 5 is the family's soft spot. A Turkish truck forum documents melted pistons on a 1846T in milk haulage, with the shop attributing it to poor fuel quality or leaking injectors, and long-running forum opinion there holds that the in-house-engined 1838T gave less trouble than the FPT-engined 1846T. Treat a 1846T with a very clean or recently resealed engine, or with new injector lines, as worth a close-up.

Same forum thread describes a post-repair rebuild going wrong on a 1846T. On any tractor of this age look for oil weeping at the rocker cover, sump rail and rear main, and for coolant staining around the radiator and hose joints.

models.segment: all-rounder tractor and chassis: semitrailer tractor, construction and municipal work. The narrow-cab sibling of the TGX, sharing its driveline and its two styling generations.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine, 2,240 mm wide - 200 mm narrower than the TGX cab, which is the surest way to tell them apart. Three cabs: TM (long, medium high, 1,690 mm standing height, up to two bunks), TN (long, standard height, 1,410 mm, one bunk), NN (medium length 1,880 mm external, standard height, no bunk - a day cab). Engine tunnel is 280 mm high against the TGX's 120 mm, so the TGS floor is noticeably humped.
models.driveline: Same Euro 6 inline-sixes as the TGX: D3066 12.7 L (380-560 PS), D2676 12.4 L (440-540 PS), D1556 9.0 L (330-400 PS). No 15.2 L D3876 in the TGS table. MAN TipMatic automated or manual.

generations.years: 2007-2020, sharing the TGX's 2012 and 2016 facelifts
visual_markers: 'MAN' wordmark in block letters across the grille with a small lion emblem directly beneath it, on a dark grille panel - note this is the reverse of the 2020 TGX, which puts the lion ABOVE the wordmark in its own chrome frame
Narrow cab: the cab sides sit close to the chassis rails and the front wheels stand proud of the cab line
Horizontal headlamp clusters in the outer bumper corners
Frequently seen with a low or medium roof and no roof spoiler, unlike the TGX

generations.years: 2020-present (new MAN Truck Generation)
visual_markers: Restyled front shared in architecture with the 2020 TGX - MAN wordmark in the grille with the lion above it in a chrome frame - but on the narrow 2,240 mm cab
Fully digital instrument cluster

known_weak_points.note: Air tanks are a named item on a used-buyer list for the TGS tipper, as they are on the TGX list. Check for crushed, scraped or re-clamped tanks and for corrosion at the cradles.
AdBlue is a named item on the same list; look for urea crystallisation around the tank cap, sender and dosing lines.
Fuel is a named item on the same list; check the tank straps, the filler neck and the area beneath the tank for diesel weeping.
Sideguards are a named item; on a tipper-spec TGS they take impact damage and are often bent, missing or replaced with non-original panels.
Engine is the first item on the list, and the TGX's D20/D26 EGR cooler weakness applies to the TGS, which uses the same D2676 and D3066 engines.

identity_tells: Chrome lion emblem, as on every MAN
Narrow cab, 2,240 mm, against the TGX's 2,440 mm; in a front-on photograph the TGS cab does not overhang the front wheels as far
A high 280 mm engine tunnel inside the cab, versus 120 mm in a TGX - visible in any interior photo as a pronounced hump between the seats
A 'TGS' badge with a tonnage.power number pair, and very often a day cab (NN) or a low roof, which the TGX range does not offer in the same form

models.segment: long-haul flagship tractor unit; the TGX cab is the wide cab of the MAN TG range. International Truck of the Year 2021 for the 2020 generation.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine. Current TGX cabs are all 2,440 mm wide and 2,280 mm long externally and differ only in roof height: GX (extra high, 2,070 mm standing height over the engine tunnel, two bunks, 355 l roof rack), GM (medium high, 1,860 mm, two bunks), GN (standard height, 1,580 mm, one bunk). Engine tunnel is a low 120 mm in all three. The 2020 cab sits 10 cm higher on the frame than the 2007-2020 one, and the largest cab no longer uses a special enlarged windscreen.
models.driveline: Inline-six diesels throughout, all Euro 6. Current range: D3876 15.2 L (540 / 580 / 640 PS), D3066 12.7 L (380-560 PS), D2676 12.4 L (440-540 PS), D1556 9.0 L (330-400 PS). Gearboxes: manual, MAN TipMatic automated, and on some models Scania Opticruise after the Traton tie-up. The 16.2 L D2868 V8 was offered from 2007 and dropped around 2012 for lack of demand, replaced by the 15.2 L D3876 six. Power was raised in steps: +20 PS / +100 Nm at the 2016 facelift (Euro 6c) and +10 PS / +100 Nm in 2019 (Euro 6d).

known_weak_points.note: A used-buyer guide for the TGX opens its list with rear air tanks fouling on trailer landing legs when the fifth-wheel position has not been checked before reversing under a trailer. Look for crushed, scraped or re-clamped air tanks behind the cab and for fresh weld or paint on the tank cradles.

MAN's own Euro 5 service advice called for extra EGR checks because high coolant temperatures raise the risk of EGR cooler leaks, and EGR cooler failure is the fault owners of D20/D26-engined TGX name most often, alongside intercoolers, compressor clutch solenoid, liners and cylinder head. A coolant loss with no external leak, or an unusually clean EGR/intercooler area, is worth a close-up. Reported through an owner group rather than measured.

models.segment: long-haul and heavy-distribution tractor unit; Mercedes-Benz's flagship heavy truck since 1996.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine. The long-haul cab family is named by space: ClassicSpace (short/day), StreamSpace, BigSpace and GigaSpace, the last two being the tall long-haul sleepers. Mercedes also splits by width - the 'L cab' proven design is 2.30 m wide, and the wide 2.5 m cab is what BigSpace and GigaSpace normally sit on. From 2024 the Actros L adds the aerodynamic ProCabin, offered as ProCabin Stream, ProCabin Big and ProCabin Giga. Older MP3-era naming used S (day/construction), M (distribution sleeper), L (low-roof long-haul) and LH MegaSpace (high-roof long-haul).
models.driveline: Inline-six Euro 6 diesels from the fourth generation on: OM471 12.8 L (about 422-530 PS) and OM473 15.6 L (about 517-625 PS), common rail at 2,800 bar with twin overhead camshafts and 24 valves. The first three generations used V-engines instead - OM501 12 L V6 (310-480 PS) and OM502 V8 (350-652 PS) - so an Actros with a V6 or V8 under the cab is an MP1/MP2/MP3, and that is a useful dating check. PowerShift automated gearbox; MP3 was the first in the segment to make an automatic standard.

visual_markers: Mirror brackets are closed-loop, adopted from the previous generation's special editions
Bi-xenon headlamps, lightly revised from MP2
A V6 or V8 engine (OM501/OM502) rather than an inline six

Grille is built from body-coloured horizontal bars over fine mesh, split into a narrow upper section carrying the star and a deeper lower mesh section
Headlamps are horizontal rectangular clusters in the outer lower corners with a small round fog lamp inboard of each
CONVENTIONAL glass door mirrors on black arms - a large main housing plus a wide-angle housing
Wraparound body-coloured bumper with a dark central step insert and licence-plate recess
Black roof-front band carrying LED marker lamps
Inline-six OM471 or OM473 under the cab, not a V-engine

generations.years: 2018-2023 (revealed September 2018 at the IAA in Hannover as the 2019 Actros)
visual_markers: MirrorCam: no glass exterior mirrors at all. Slim black camera arms are mounted at the top of each A-pillar and arc outward and downward. This is the single most decisive Actros dating tell in a photograph - MirrorCam means MP5 or later, glass mirrors mean MP4 or earlier
Interior: two colour displays - a touchscreen and an instrument display behind the wheel - replacing the conventional analogue cluster, plus two vertical MirrorCam screens on the A-pillars
Grille architecture is carried over from MP4 (star in a ring, Actros script beside it) so the front alone is a weak discriminator; check the mirrors

visual_markers: ProCabin: the front grille is 80 mm longer than the previous cab and the bumper is reshaped around it, so the nose reads as visibly deeper
Sold as ProCabin Stream, Big and Giga

known_weak_points.note: The Euro 6 SCR system is the Actros's most-reported weak area: NOx sensor failures and AdBlue dosing-injector crystallisation, the latter brought on by off-spec urea or short runs that never heat the system through. An in-tank AdBlue heater element burnout is also documented and can let the solution gel and crack the tank or dosing lines. Look for white urea crystallisation around the dosing injector and tank fittings, and for a wet or stained AdBlue tank seam.

DPF blocking is one of the commonest reasons an Actros shows a warning lamp, on trucks doing short regional or urban cycles rather than steady highway kilometres. Sticking EGR valves and faulty exhaust temperature sensors also produce spurious DPF warnings. A recently replaced or exchanged DPF canister on an otherwise weathered exhaust is worth noting.

OM471-specific: injector tip wear on high-kilometre trucks without service history (black smoke and rising consumption), fuel rail pressure sensor faults, and EGR valve carbon sticking. Reconditioning shops also list injector leakage, turbo wear, oil pressure loss, camshaft wear, piston ring degradation, cylinder scoring and excessive crankcase pressure as the OM471 jobs they see.

Early MP4 production (roughly pre-2014) has a documented water-ingress problem where moisture tracks down the wiring looms to the ECUs, corroding connector pins and producing intermittent engine management, instrument cluster and PSM faults; some trucks needed a full engine harness. On a high-kilometre MP4, a cluster with lit or flickering warnings is worth more weight than on other makes.

The EBS itself is reliable; the reported faults are wheel speed sensors fouled by brake dust setting ABS/EBS codes. On a high-kilometre truck also check air dryer cartridge condition and brake adjusters.
Wiper motor failure is a recurring minor fleet complaint on high-kilometre MP4s, and the instrument cluster is one of the units affected by the early-MP4 loom water ingress.

generations.years: 2012-2021 (Stralis Hi-Range, Euro 6, International Truck of the Year 2013 as Hi-Way)

models.segment: long-haul tractor unit. R is the high forward-control cab; S, added in 2016, is the flat-floor flagship above it. Both sit in Scania's modular PRT range alongside the lower P, G and L cabs.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine, fully modular. First-generation R (2004-2017) was offered with Highline and Topline roofs and, from 2013, in aerodynamic Streamline form. The second generation, launched 23 August 2016, brought a new R sleeper cab and the all-new S-series, which is the first Scania with a genuinely flat interior floor - no engine tunnel to step over. The low-entry L-series followed in December 2017.
models.driveline: Inline-sixes and V8s across the modular range: DC09 9.3 L I5, DC11 10.6 L I6, DC13 12.7 L I6, DC16 15.6 / 16.4 L V8, with range-wide outputs from about 220 to 770 hp. Manual was standard on the first generation; Scania Opticruise automated is standard on the second. In April 2010 the V8 reached 730 hp and 3,500 Nm. The second generation added two touchscreen infotainment packages, 5-inch base and 7-inch premium, with CarPlay from April 2017.

generations.years: 2004-2017, with a significant restyle in September 2009 and the Streamline aerodynamic version from March 2013
visual_markers: Grille is a body-coloured panel with a horizontal chrome bar carrying the Scania griffin badge, and the SCANIA wordmark is NOT spelled out across a black grille panel
The September 2009 upgrade gave sharper exterior styling with visibly larger grille openings; the front air filter grilles on G and R were redesigned again in 2014
Front air-intake grille panels flank the main grille at the cab corners

generations.years: 2016-present (R and S launched 23 August 2016 at the Grand Palais, Paris; cab developed with Porsche Engineering)
visual_markers: 'SCANIA' in large light-coloured block capitals across the top of a black grille panel, with the griffin badge to the right of the wordmark
Below the wordmark, three broad horizontal black slat bars with mesh behind, inside a body-coloured surround
Headlamps are angular units at the outer lower corners with a hooked LED daytime-running signature running along the outer edge
Model designation such as 'R 500' or 'S 730' printed small on the lower front panel beside the headlamp

S versus R at a glance: the S cab front is deeper and flatter and its lower edge sits higher off the road, with no step recess cut into the centre of the bumper - the R keeps a stepped centre bumper because it still has a cab floor to climb into. In a straight-on pair photograph the S's grille sits visibly higher than the R's

known_weak_points.note: The first item on a used-buyer list for the R-series is wiring between the door and the mirror, which corrodes and chafes where the loom passes through the door mirror. Check the rubber grommet at the mirror arm and the mirror housing for a repaired or taped loom.
Seats are the second named item; on a high-mileage R the driver's seat bolster and base wear is a recognised inspection point.
The stereo/head unit is the third named item on the same list.

identity_tells: The Scania griffin badge - a crowned griffin head in a red roundel or on a chrome bar
'SCANIA' spelled out in block capitals across a black grille means the 2016-onward generation; a chrome bar with a griffin and no wordmark means 2004-2017
Model designation is a letter and a number - R 450, S 500 - where the letter is the cab family and the number the horsepower, unlike the German makers' tonnage.power pairs
A flat cab floor with no engine tunnel means an S-series; any Scania with a step up into the cab interior from the door sill is an R, G, P or L
V8 models carry a V8 badge on the cab side and are the only V8s left in this class

models.segment: long-haul tractor unit; DAF's flagship cab-over since 1997 and a three-time International Truck of the Year (XF105 in 2007, XF106 in 2018, New Generation XF in 2022).
models.cab: Cab-over-engine. Roof variants are named Space Cab and Super Space Cab (and Space Cab Plus). From the 2021 New Generation the larger cabs were split off under their own model names, XG and XG+, leaving XF as the shorter-cab designation - so on a 2021-or-later truck, XF, XG and XG+ are three different cab sizes rather than trim levels.
models.driveline: PACCAR MX-11 10.8 L and PACCAR MX-13 12.9 L inline-sixes, with ZF AS Tronic or ZF Traxon gearboxes in manual and automated form; 330-390 kW for the combustion models. Shares its chassis family with the DAF CF.

generations.years: 2005-2012 (International Truck of the Year 2007)
visual_markers: 'DAF' in block letters at the LEFT of the lower cab panel and 'XF' at the RIGHT, split apart across the panel rather than grouped in a grille
A small DAF diamond badge - a triangle inside a diamond outline - near the bottom right of the cab panel
The upper grille is a body-coloured panel with horizontal louvres; the black slatted grille sits below it in the bumper
Large rectangular headlamp clusters in the bumper corners
Flat, square cab front with no rounding at the corners
'DAF' moulded into the mudflaps

generations.years: 2013-2021 (Euro 6, International Truck of the Year 2018)
visual_markers: Restyled front over the XF105, with a larger dark grille area, but still the flat square cab front and the split DAF/XF lettering on the cab panel rather than a wordmark inside the grille

generations.years: 2021-present (New Generation; larger cabs renamed XG and XG+)
visual_markers: 'DAF' in large silver block capitals sits INSIDE the grille at the top, with horizontal slats stepping down beneath it - the lettering has moved off the body panel and into the grille
Cab front and A-pillars are visibly rounded and the nose is longer, a consequence of the new EU length rules; the flat square face of the XF105/XF106 is gone
Headlamps are slim angular units at the outer lower corners with an amber indicator section
Power figure printed small at the bottom of the grille, e.g. '530'
'XF' badge high on the cab side behind the door - on this generation that badge is a cab-size statement, not just a range name, because the taller cabs say XG or XG+
Slim body-coloured mirror housings mounted low on the door

known_weak_points.note: Hub seals and brake discs are the first two items on a used-buyer list for the XF. Look for oil tracking from the hub onto the inside of the wheel and drum/disc face, and for heat cracking or a deep lip on the disc.
The rear axle modulator valve is a named item; check for corrosion at the valve body and for chafed or re-routed air lines to the rear axle.
NOx sensors and exhaust heat shields are both named items. A missing or rattling heat shield and a recently replaced NOx sensor are both visible from underneath.
A gauge-related item appears on the same list.

identity_tells: DAF diamond emblem, and the DAF wordmark - on the cab panel before 2021, inside the grille from 2021
'XF', 'XG' or 'XG+' badge on the cab side behind the door; from 2021 these are three cab sizes on the same truck
Model number in the form XF 105.460 on the older trucks: 105 is the range and 460 the power in PS; the newer trucks simply say XF 480 or XF 530
A rounded, long nose with DAF written inside the grille dates the truck to 2021 or later; a flat square face with DAF and XF split across the cab panel is 2005-2021

models.segment: long-haul tractor unit; Volvo's flagship cab-over since 1993.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine, offered as Sleeper, Globetrotter, Globetrotter XL and Globetrotter XXL. The cab is built at Umea from hot-dip galvanised high-tensile steel, which is worth knowing when judging corrosion on an older example.
models.driveline: Inline-six turbodiesel with intercooler throughout, historically badged by displacement (FH12 12.1 L, FH13 13 L, FH16 16 L). Volvo's own D-series engines; 14-speed synchro-manual gearboxes in the early cars and I-Shift automated later. In September 2011 the FH16 750 became the most powerful large-scale production truck at 750 hp and 3,550 Nm.

generations.years: 2012-present. Volvo re-launched the FH in September 2012 with significant technology upgrades; this is the cab most Turkish and European used listings from 2013 onward show
visual_markers: The grille is crossed by the Volvo signature diagonal slash with the round Volvo iron-mark roundel set into it, offset from centre - no other maker in the class uses a diagonal grille bar
Cab front is V-sculpted: the grille slats angle down toward a central point
Cab name spelled out on the black band across the roof front: 'GLOBETROTTER'
Model number badge on the cab side behind the door, e.g. '500', above a chrome underline
Headlamps are large angular units at the outer corners with an upward-swept outer edge

known_weak_points.note: The first item on a used-buyer list for the FH is seals: poor window seals that whistle at speed. Check the windscreen and side-window rubbers for perishing, lifting and past resealing.
Leaking door seals are named in the same first item; look for water staining down the inside of the door card and a discoloured or displaced door rubber.

The cab tilt cylinder is named alongside the seals. A leaking tilt ram leaves hydraulic oil on the chassis rail and the back of the front crossmember - visible in almost any low front-three-quarter photograph.

identity_tells: The circular Volvo iron mark on a diagonal bar crossing the grille
GLOBETROTTER or GLOBETROTTER XL spelled out on the roof-front band - that band names the cab variant directly
Model badge is a bare power figure (460, 500, 540, 750) on the cab side rather than a tonnage.power pair
FH12 / FH13 / FH16 badging on older trucks names the engine displacement, so it dates and specifies the truck at once

models.segment: long-haul tractor unit; replaced the Renault Premium and Magnum together. International Truck of the Year 2015.
models.cab: Cab-over-engine, offered as Day Cab, Night & Day Cab, Sleeper Cab and High Sleeper Cab. The tall long-haul version is badged T High, and the largest living space is the Maxispace.
models.driveline: Two Euro VI inline-sixes: DTI 11 (11 L, 380 / 430 / 460 hp) and DTI 13 (13 L, 440 / 480 / 520 hp), with the robotised 12-speed Optidriver automated gearbox as standard. The T was designed by Herve Bertrand and shares some parts with the contemporary Volvo FH - Renault Trucks has been part of the Volvo Group since 2001 - so a Renault T and a Volvo FH of the same year can share chassis and driveline components while looking nothing alike.

generations.years: 2013-present (presented 11 June 2013, on sale from the end of 2013)
visual_markers: A steeply raked, forward-leaning windscreen - the T's cab front slopes back far more than any German rival's and is the quickest way to spot one at distance
Renault's diamond/lozenge emblem centred in a narrow black lower grille, beneath a broad body-coloured upper panel
Headlamps are large angular wrap-around units at the outer corners carrying an amber indicator lens within the cluster
Two-tier front: a body-coloured upper bumper band above a dark grille and valance
Cab variant written on the front plate area or lower door, e.g. 'T HIGH MAXISPACE'

known_weak_points.note: The first item on a used-buyer list for the Range T is the rear mudguards and their brackets, which are prone to failure. A drooping, cracked or missing rear mudguard on a T is a known model fault rather than a one-off impact.
The second item is the exterior steps, described as flimsy and prone to damage on early models. Check the step treads and their mounting brackets for bending and for repair welds.

identity_tells: Renault diamond emblem in the grille
The strongly inclined windscreen and wedge-shaped cab front
Badging is a bare power figure after the letter - T 460, T 480, T 520
'T HIGH' on a tall cab identifies the long-haul roof variant
